sections.title: The Spies Sent to Jericho
observations: In this section, we see Joshua sending two spies to scout the land, particularly Jericho. This act demonstrates Joshua's leadership and strategic planning as he prepares the Israelites to enter the Promised Land.

The choice of spies reflects a continuation of the previous generation's experience, but with a different outcome in mind. Unlike the twelve spies sent by Moses, these two are not named, emphasizing their role as instruments of God's plan rather than individual heroes.

sections.title: Rahab's Faith and Deception
observations: Rahab, a Canaanite prostitute, plays a crucial role in this narrative. Her faith in the God of Israel is evident as she hides the spies and acknowledges the power of the Lord.

This section highlights the theme of God's grace and inclusion, as Rahab, despite her background, becomes a key figure in the lineage of Christ. Her actions demonstrate that faith can be found in unexpected places.

sections.title: The Covenant of Protection
observations: The spies make a covenant with Rahab, promising to spare her and her family during the conquest of Jericho. This agreement underscores the importance of faith and obedience to God's commands.

Rahab's request for protection illustrates her understanding of the impending judgment on Jericho and her desire to be saved. It also reflects the broader theme of redemption that runs throughout Scripture.

sections.title: The Spies' Escape and Report
observations: The spies' escape from Jericho and their report back to Joshua serve as a pivotal moment in the narrative. They bring back a positive report, contrasting the fear and doubt of the previous generation's spies.
This section emphasizes the importance of faith in God's promises and the assurance that He is with His people as they face challenges ahead.

importantVerses.commentary: Rahab's declaration of faith in the God of Israel highlights the recognition of God's sovereignty and power among the nations.
Rahab's commitment to the spies and her family signifies the importance of faith and the covenant relationship with God.

questions: What does Rahab's story teach us about faith and redemption?
How does the sending of the spies reflect God's guidance in our decision-making?
In what ways can we see God's sovereignty at work in the events of this chapter?
